checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is cross-client state root consensus maintained for all Osaka state transitions?

audit_items.state_context: Prysm consensus client. Fulu fork epoch = math.MaxUint64 on mainnet (not yet activated). State root computed via HashTreeRoot(), compared against block's signed state_root field. Version mismatch guard prevents cross-version transitions.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Prysm computes beacon state roots via st.HashTreeRoot(ctx) and validates against the block's signed state_root field. Fulu fork is gated behind FuluForkEpoch = math.MaxUint64 on mainnet — no Fulu state transitions are currently reachable. Version mismatch guard (st.Version() != signed.Block().Version()) prevents invalid cross-fork transitions. validateExecutionAndConsensus runs consensus and execution validation concurrently via errgroup on disjoint data with no race on state root computation. The next-slot cache is root-keyed with rollback on error, preventing stale state issues.
anomalies: Fulu-specific state transition logic is defined but FuluForkEpoch=MaxUint64 prevents activation on mainnet
When Fulu is activated, any divergence in Fulu epoch processing (PeerDAS data columns, new operations) could cause cross-client state root mismatch
Cross-client testing at the Fulu activation boundary is a future risk
phase1_abstract_interpretation.attack_surface: Currently inactive (Fulu not yet scheduled). Future risk at activation.

scenarios_tested.scenario: Fulu state transition with divergent client implementations
scenarios_tested.result: Not reachable: FuluForkEpoch = math.MaxUint64 on mainnet
Guard present: st.Version() check prevents cross-version transitions

scenarios_tested.scenario: Cache stale state causing root divergence
scenarios_tested.result: Cache is root-keyed; rollback on error prevents stale state propagation

phase2_5_invariant_candidates: For all activated fork versions, beacon state HashTreeRoot() must equal the state_root field in accepted blocks
Fulu epoch processing must produce identical results across all client implementations

phase3_invariant_proving.justification: The state root check is structurally sound for all currently-activated forks. Fulu code paths do not modify beacon state fields included in the state root for currently-reachable code paths. The invariant holds for all reachable inputs at present. When Fulu is activated, cross-client testing will be required to verify consensus on new state transition operations.
phase3_invariant_proving.residual_risk: Future activation of Fulu introduces cross-client consensus risk that cannot be statically verified in a single-client audit

phase3_5_bug_bounty_assessment.reasoning: The state root consensus check is properly implemented in Prysm for all currently-activated forks. Fulu is not yet scheduled on mainnet (epoch = MaxUint64). The check is out-of-scope for static single-client analysis as it requires multi-client interoperability testing.

audit_items.notes: Prysm correctly implements beacon state root validation. Fulu not yet activated on mainnet. Cross-client consensus testing required when Fulu is scheduled. The 16777216 value in Prysm is HISTORICAL_ROOTS_LIMIT, unrelated to EIP-7825 gas cap.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is transaction gasLimit > 16777216 rejected at txpool admission?

code_scope.resolution_error: Prysm has no txpool implementation. EIP-7825 txpool gas cap enforcement is an execution layer concern.

audit_items.state_context: Prysm is a consensus layer (beacon chain) client. It has no transaction pool, no transaction admission control, and no per-transaction gas limit validation. Transaction validation is entirely delegated to the execution client via Engine API.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Prysm does not implement a txpool. The EIP-7825 property requires rejection of transactions with gasLimit > 16777216 at txpool admission. This is an execution layer responsibility (Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Reth, Erigon). Prysm has no code path that touches per-transaction gas limits.

phase2_symbolic_execution.note: No code to analyze in Prysm for this property

phase3_invariant_proving.justification: Out of scope for Prysm. Recommend evaluation against the paired execution client.

phase3_5_bug_bounty_assessment.reasoning: Prysm is a consensus layer client with no txpool. EIP-7825 enforcement is an execution layer responsibility. No code to audit in Prysm for this property.

audit_items.notes: EIP-7825 txpool enforcement is not in scope for Prysm (consensus client). Evaluate against execution layer clients.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is GAS_CAP constant exactly 16777216 (2^24)?

code_scope.resolution_error: No GAS_CAP constant in Prysm. The 16777216 value is HistoricalRootsLength (beacon state parameter), not EIP-7825 gas cap.

audit_items.state_context: Prysm is a consensus layer client. The EIP-7825 GAS_CAP constant belongs to the execution layer. The numerical coincidence of 16777216 (2^24) appearing as HISTORICAL_ROOTS_LIMIT in Prysm is unrelated to EIP-7825.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: No GAS_CAP constant with EIP-7825 semantics exists in Prysm. The 16777216 value in config/fieldparams/mainnet.go:10 is HISTORICAL_ROOTS_LIMIT — a beacon state SSZ list length limit with different semantics. Thorough search confirms no per-transaction gas cap constant anywhere in the codebase.
anomalies: Potential confusion: 16777216 appears in Prysm with different semantics (HISTORICAL_ROOTS_LIMIT) than EIP-7825 (GAS_CAP). These are unrelated constants that happen to share the same numeric value.

phase2_symbolic_execution.note: No EIP-7825 gas cap constant to verify in Prysm

phase3_invariant_proving.justification: Out of scope. EIP-7825 GAS_CAP is an execution layer constant.

phase3_5_bug_bounty_assessment.reasoning: No GAS_CAP constant in Prysm. The HistoricalRootsLength=16777216 is a different parameter with different semantics. Out of scope for Prysm audit.

audit_items.notes: No EIP-7825 GAS_CAP constant in Prysm. The 16777216 in Prysm is HISTORICAL_ROOTS_LIMIT (beacon state). Evaluate against execution layer clients.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is tx gas cap independent from block gas limit?

code_scope.resolution_error: Prysm does not validate per-transaction gas limits. Block gas limit (execution payload GasLimit field) is accepted from the execution client without independence checking against a per-tx cap.

audit_items.state_context: Prysm validates only the block-level GasLimit field (must not be zero). Per-transaction gas caps are not validated. Execution payload is treated as opaque by Prysm — all per-tx validation is delegated to the execution client.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Prysm has no code enforcing independence between tx gas cap and block gas limit. The block-level payload.GasLimit() is validated only for non-zero value (log.go:138-141). No code iterates over transactions or checks individual gasLimit fields. The independence property (EIP-7825) must be enforced by the execution client.

phase2_symbolic_execution.note: No per-tx gas validation code in Prysm to analyze

phase3_invariant_proving.justification: Out of scope for Prysm. Independence check is an execution layer responsibility.

phase3_5_bug_bounty_assessment.reasoning: No per-tx gas cap validation in Prysm by design. EIP-7825 independence property is an execution layer concern. Prysm correctly delegates this to the execution client via Engine API.

audit_items.notes: Prysm only validates block-level GasLimit != 0. Per-tx gas cap independence is an execution layer concern. Evaluate against execution clients.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does block validation iterate ALL transactions for gas cap check?

audit_items.state_context: Prysm's block validation delegates execution payload validation entirely to the execution client via Engine API (engine_newPayloadV4/V5). The transaction list is opaque to Prysm — it is SSZ-encoded/decoded as bytes but individual transaction fields (gasLimit, gasPrice, etc.) are never inspected. The only 'transaction' interaction is in log.go which calls p.Transactions() purely for logging the count.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Prysm does NOT iterate over transactions for gas cap validation. The entire execution payload, including all transactions, is forwarded to the execution client via engine_newPayloadV* API call. Prysm accepts VALID/INVALID/SYNCING responses and acts accordingly. If the execution client incorrectly accepts a payload containing transactions with gasLimit > 16777216, Prysm has zero independent defense — this is an architectural design choice. The 'Transactions()' call in log.go:51 is for logging only (counting txs), never for validation.
anomalies: ARCHITECTURAL GAP: Prysm completely trusts the execution client for transaction-level validation. A malicious or buggy execution client returning VALID for a block with oversized transaction gas limits would result in Prysm accepting the invalid block.
No defense-in-depth for EIP-7825 violations at the consensus layer — consistent with separation of concerns but creates a single point of failure at the execution layer
phase1_abstract_interpretation.attack_surface: If an execution client has a bug in EIP-7825 enforcement, Prysm provides no fallback validation. This is an architectural limitation shared by all consensus layer clients.

scenarios_tested.scenario: Block payload with last transaction having gasLimit = 16777217 (oversized)
scenarios_tested.result: Prysm would forward to execution client unchanged. Execution client returns VALID/INVALID. Prysm takes no independent action.
scenarios_tested.note: Exploitation depends on execution client having EIP-7825 bug, not on Prysm

scenarios_tested.scenario: Block payload with first N-1 valid txs and Nth tx oversized
scenarios_tested.result: Same as above — Prysm does not iterate, so position is irrelevant

phase2_5_invariant_candidates: If execution client returns VALID, all transactions in payload satisfy EIP-7825 gas cap (cannot be verified in Prysm independently)

phase3_invariant_proving.justification: From Prysm's perspective, there are NO guards for per-transaction gas cap checking. This is not a Prysm bug — it is by design (separation of concerns). The invariant must be proven at the execution layer. However, the lack of any independent verification means Prysm cannot detect execution client bugs in EIP-7825 enforcement.
phase3_invariant_proving.residual_risk: Single point of failure at execution layer. If execution client fails to reject oversized tx, consensus client has no fallback.

phase3_5_bug_bounty_assessment.reasoning: Prysm correctly delegates execution payload validation to the execution client by design. The lack of per-transaction gas cap checking in Prysm is not a vulnerability in Prysm — it is the expected architecture. The EIP-7825 check must be evaluated at the execution client layer. Note the architectural observation that Prysm provides no defense-in-depth for this property.

audit_items.notes: Prysm delegates all per-transaction validation to execution client via Engine API. This is correct architecture. EIP-7825 block validation (iterating all txs) must be audited in execution layer clients (Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Reth, Erigon). Architectural note: Prysm provides zero defense-in-depth for EIP-7825 — if execution client has a bug, consensus client cannot catch it.
